headline: Monitor Backcountry and Campsite Booking Windows
reservation: Strathcona requires distinct planning for front-country campgrounds versus backcountry wilderness permits via the BC Parks portal. Popular sites like Buttle Lake book up months in advance, and policies for trailhead parking or remote access can change; always verify the current year’s reservation windows before departing Campbell River.

days.title: Subalpine Peaks and Valleys

stops.name: Paradise Meadows
stops.detail: Traverse the accessible boardwalks of the Forbidden Plateau to view subalpine wildflowers and small mountain lakes.

stops.name: Mount Albert Edward Trailhead
stops.detail: Begin the ascent toward the park's higher elevations for sweeping views of the Vancouver Island interior.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour to the Forbidden Plateau area; conditions vary with mountain weather.
days.note: The higher elevations are subject to snowpack late into July; check trail reports.

days.title: Buttle Lake Glacial Waters
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Buttle Lake Campground

stops.name: Myra Falls
stops.detail: Visit the multi-tiered cascades where the creek meets the southern end of the lake.

stops.name: Lupin Falls
stops.detail: Take the short forested loop to see this narrow ribbon waterfall through ancient cedar groves.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for travel along the lake; logging roads may be active.
days.note: Buttle Lake can experience high winds in the afternoon, affecting small watercraft.

days.title: Deep Wilderness and Western Valleys
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Gold River Gateway

stops.name: Lady Falls
stops.detail: Witness the powerful 30-meter drop from the viewing platform nestled in old-growth forest.

stops.name: Elk River Trailhead
stops.detail: Hike into the rugged glacial valley flanked by Colonel Foster and Landslide Lake.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for variable paved and gravel surfaces; conditions vary.
days.note: Cellular reception is non-existent in the western valleys; prepare for self-sufficiency.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: The Paradise Meadows lot often reaches capacity during peak summer weekends. Arrive at these high-elevation gateways early to ensure a spot before the midday influx.

intel.title: Mountain Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is lost shortly after leaving Campbell River or Gold River. Download all navigation maps offline as the interior peaks block most cellular frequencies.

intel.title: Gateway Provisions
intel.text: Campbell River serves as the primary hub for fuel and supplies before entering the park interior. There are no refueling services within the park boundaries or at Buttle Lake.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Access
intel.text: Access roads to the Forbidden Plateau may be gated during the off-season. Consult the official BC Parks page for seasonal opening and closing dates for the Strathcona Parkway.

intel.title: Backcountry Permits
intel.text: Backcountry camping requires registration via the BC Parks website. Ensure you have proof of registration for sites within the Forbidden Plateau or along the Elk River.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Campbell River Airport (YBL), secure groceries in Campbell River, and head west via Highway 28.
plan.vehicle: A standard car suffices for paved park roads, but high-clearance is advised for unpaved logging spurs; check rental insurance for gravel road coverage.
plan.goldenHour: Buttle Lake shorelines offer reflective views at sunset, though shadows fall early due to steep surrounding peaks.
